items.title: Why Japan’s markets flipped the usual script after central bank rate hike
items.body: The yen weakened past 157 against the dollar, the yield on the 10-year Japanese Government Bond slipped, while the Nikkei 225 gained 1.5%.

items.title: France’s wine production nears a 70-year low, leaving winemakers with tough choices
items.body: As the French wine industry reaches a crisis point, key players are considering new markets, products and generations.

items.title: Consumer sentiment is in the dumps despite a solid economy. Goldman Sachs blames 'lower happiness'
items.body: Goldman economist Joseph Briggs said broader pessimism in society may be contributing to struggling consumer sentiment even as the economy chugs along.

items.title: Bank of England defies Fed’s rate-hike lead, leaving rates unchanged
items.body: The Bank of England kept rates steady Thursday, even after U.K. inflation rose to 3.1% and energy costs put pressure on prices.

items.title: UK inflation jumps to 3.1% as energy costs soar
items.body: The reading comes a day before the Bank of England updates its monetary policy.

items.title: 'Science fiction': Transport companies — the backbone of economy — are sounding alarm on fuel prices
items.body: Prices for diesel, the fuel type used to power trucks and trains, came in at an all-time high of $6.31 per gallon on Wednesday.

items.title: Consumers hit by one-two punch of oil and rates from Iran war. The estimated bill is $1,700 per household
items.body: Rising oil prices and Treasury yields are lifting energy and borrowing costs for U.S. households, pushing consumers to draw more heavily on savings.

items.title: Indonesia's new finance minister faces an uphill battle on fiscal credibility
items.body: Nazara, sworn in hours after Purbaya's dismissal, spent seven years as deputy finance minister and led the ministry's fiscal policy agency from 2015 to 2019.
